turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Sure! Let me solve one first and think out loud.
I work every day. My brother works every day.
Step 1: I check who does it. "My brother" is one person, a "he".
Step 2: So I add -s to the verb: work becomes works.
The rule: after he, she or it, add -s to the verb.
Right: She works in a shop. Wrong: She work in a shop.

Now it's your turn. Write only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
turns.judgeInput:

W1 (wrong) strength 2: the verb does not change after he/she/it. Its error: leaves the verb unchanged after he/she/it ("She like tea").
W2 (wrong) strength 1: -s goes on every verb and -es/-ies are not needed. Its error: adds -s wrongly or misspells -es/-ies ("She watchs TV", "I plays").
C1 (correct) strength 1: add -s/-es after he/she/it. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
C2 (correct) strength 0: -es after sh/ch/s/x/o, -ies after consonant + y, no -s after I/you/we/they. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
